Rae (Design): dropped a quick mock of the playground preview behavior when a tool call returns structured rows + a small action bar: https://figma.com/file/new-preview (preview) Rae (Design): problem: users scan the preview but don't realize they can take actions (copy, open in table viewer, map to schema). need a discoverable affordance. Ibrahim (DevEx): saw support note: people expected the preview to be read-only. Suggestion: surface 1-2 primary actions inline and collapse the rest under kebab. Clara (Frontend): implementation idea: show a thin action strip that appears on hover/focus with icons + accessible labels. HTML-ish mock: ```html 
[ { name: "A" }, ... ]
``` Owen (A11y): a couple of things: action strip must be keyboard reachable without hover; put it after the preview in DOM so tab order is predictable. Also ensure each action has clear text or aria-label. Avoid hiding interactive controls with CSS-only hover. Tess (PM): telemetry ask: record action clicks + whether users first expanded preview before acting. events: `preview_open`, `preview_action_click` with action type. Rae (Design): copy micro-nit: labels should be verbs: "Open table", "Copy JSON", "Map schema" — clearer than nouns. add a confirmation toast for mapping actions. Ibrahim (DevEx): guardrails: if payload > 200KB, disable "Open table" and show hint "Large payload: open in new tab" to avoid browser OOM. Clara (Frontend): noted. For streaming payloads, we should keep action strip visible but disable "Copy" until first chunk completes; use aria-disabled and tooltip "waiting for complete payload". Owen (A11y): for screen readers, announce when actions change state: use aria-live="polite" to say "Copy enabled" rather than verbosely announcing chunks. Also ensure any toasts are announced once. Rae (Design): visual affordance: small chevron + "Open" primary button on the right of the card for quick discovery; secondary actions hidden behind kebab. will share two mocks (inline strip and right-edge CTA). Tess (PM): quick poll: react :thumbsup: for inline strip, :eyes: for right-edge CTA. Need a quick decision for the alpha build. Clara (Frontend): :thumbsup: Owen (A11y): :thumbsup: Ibrahim (DevEx): :eyes: (lean CTA but ok with strip) Tess (PM): :thumbsup: Rae (Design): I'll upload final frames and a short keyboard test script. tagging @Owen for a11y sign-off before PR. deploy-bot: preview deployed to staging at https://staging.playground/redwood/preview-2060004321 :rocket:
